papers.title: OPTIMIZING CLOUD RESOURCE ALLOCATION USING MULTI AGENT DEEP REINFORCEMENT LEARNING-BASED ADAPTIVE HHO ALGORITHM
papers.abstract: Cloud computing workloads are projected to grow by 23.1% annually, with over 80% of enterprises adopting multi-cloud strategies, creating a pressing need for optimal virtual machine (VM) resource allocation to ensure cost efficiency and performance. However, existing allocation strategies suffer from static optimization limitations and inefficient adaptation to dynamic workloads, leading to frequent resource underutilization and service delays. To address these issues, this work proposes a novel Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Adaptive Harris Hawks Optimization (MADRL-AHHO) algorithm for cloud resource allocation using the VM Resource Allocation dataset (VM-0 to VM-5 classes). Initially, the dataset is preprocessed through normalization and feature selection to reduce dimensionality and noise. Feature extraction is enhanced using a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) integrated with Firefly Optimization (CNN-FFO), which is benchmarked for learning capacity and solution convergence. However, performance limitations in CNN-FFO under dynamic load conditions are overcome by integrating CNN with Adaptive Harris Hawks Optimization (CNN-AHHO), which dynamically adjusts its exploration and exploitation capabilities based on multi-agent reinforcement feedback. The agents interact with the environment to learn optimal VM allocation policies by maximizing resource utilization and minimizing SLA violations. Experimental results demonstrate that CNN-AHHO outperforms CNN-FFO and traditional machine learning methods in terms of allocation accuracy, convergence rate, and computational efficiency, thereby offering a robust and adaptive solution for cloud infrastructure management.

papers.title: Transformer-Based Scalable Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Joint Resource Optimization in Cloud–Edge–End Video Streaming Systems
papers.abstract: Cloud-edge-end (CEE) collaboration has demonstrated significant potential in video streaming analysis. However, dynamic wireless environments, lack of incentive mechanisms, and constrained resources (e.g., transmission power, bandwidth, and computing resources) remain the primary bottlenecks for achieving efficient CEE-based video processing. To address these challenges, this paper focuses on a multi-user CEE scenario with dynamic wireless channels and investigates the joint optimization of adaptive incentives, cooperative offloading, and resource allocation. We propose a novel framework, called JROC, to motivate edge devices (EDs) to participate in collaborative computation within CEE, thereby enhancing system utility. Specifically, JROC encompasses a smart contract-based adaptive incentive mechanism and an Adaptive Transformer-based multi-agent reinforcement Learning Algorithm (ATLA). The incentive mechanism leverages blockchain to ensure trustworthy and automated incentive distribution, while ATLA captures long-term dependencies and global state features among agents to guide video tasks in dynamic environments through adaptive compression, cooperative offloading, and resource allocation. Moreover, we discuss key steps for deploying the proposed algorithm in a real CEE prototype, including lightweight actor inference at the terminal side and training at the edge. Experimental results based on a real-world operator dataset show that, compared to existing methods, JROC achieves higher long-term system utility while maintaining favorable scalability, thereby validating its effectiveness in resource-constrained and under-incentivized CEE video streaming scenarios.

papers.title: Mobility-Aware Resource Allocation for mmWave IAB Networks: A Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Approach
papers.abstract: MmWaves have been envisioned as a promising direction to provide Gbps wireless access. However, they are susceptible to high path losses and blockages, which directional antennas can only partially mitigate. That makes mmWave networks coverage-limited, thus requiring dense deployments. Integrated access and backhaul (IAB) architectures have emerged as a cost-effective solution for network densification. Resource allocation in mmWave IAB networks must face big challenges to cope with heavy temporal dynamics, such as intermittent links caused by user mobility and blockages from moving obstacles. This makes it extremely difficult to find optimal and adaptive solutions. In this article, exploiting the distributed structure of the problem, we propose a Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework to optimize user throughput via flow routing and link scheduling in mmWave IAB networks characterized by user mobility and link outages generated by moving obstacles. The proposed approach implicitly captures the environment dynamics, coordinates the interference, and manages the buffer levels of IAB relay nodes. We design different MARL components, considering full-duplex and half-duplex IAB-nodes. In addition, we provide a communication and coordination scheme for RL agents in an online training framework, addressing the feasibility issues of practical systems. Numerical results show the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

papers.title: Efficient Resource Allocation for On-Demand Mobile-Edge Cloud Computing
papers.abstract: Mobile-edge cloud computing is a new paradigm to provide cloud computing capabilities at the edge of pervasive radio access networks in close proximity to mobile users. Aiming at provisioning flexible on-demand mobile-edge cloud service, in this paper we propose a comprehensive framework consisting of a resource-efficient computation offloading mechanism for users and a joint communication and computation (JCC) resource allocation mechanism for network operator. Specifically, we first study the resource-efficient computation offloading problem for a user, in order to reduce user's resource occupation by determining its optimal communication and computation resource profile with minimum resource occupation and meanwhile satisfying the QoS constraint. We then tackle the critical problem of user admission control for JCC resource allocation, in order to properly select the set of users for resource demand satisfaction. We show the admission control problem is NP-hard, and hence develop an efficient approximation solution of a low complexity by carefully designing the user ranking criteria and rigourously derive its performance guarantee. To prevent the manipulation that some users may untruthfully report their valuations in acquiring mobile-edge cloud service, we further resort to the powerful tool of critical value approach to design truthful pricing scheme for JCC resource allocation. Extensive performance evaluation demonstrates that the proposed schemes can achieve superior performance for on-demand mobile-edge cloud computing.

summary: The literature on Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) for dynamic resource allocation in cloud computing emphasizes the development of adaptive frameworks to optimize resource utilization in both cloud and edge environments. Key studies highlight the limitations of static strategies and the need for innovative algorithms that can effectively manage dynamic workloads, user mobility, and link outages. Notably, gaps remain in the scalability of proposed solutions and their real-world applicability, suggesting a need for further exploration of hybrid approaches and incentive mechanisms to enhance collaboration and efficiency in resource allocation.
scholarly_positioning: Prior approaches to resource allocation in cloud computing using Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) have predominantly focused on static optimization strategies, which fail to adapt to the dynamic nature of workloads and user mobility. While recent studies have introduced innovative frameworks, they often overlook the complexities of real-world implementation and scalability, particularly in mobile-edge environments. This research aims to address these unresolved tensions by proposing a novel adaptive MARL framework that integrates hybrid optimization techniques and incentive mechanisms, thereby enhancing resource utilization and collaboration. By situating this work within the broader discourse on dynamic resource management, it seeks to contribute significantly to the understanding and application of MARL in cloud computing contexts, ultimately addressing the critical gap of effective real-time resource allocation.

research_scope: This empirical study will investigate the effectiveness of an adaptive Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework integrated with hybrid optimization techniques and incentive mechanisms for dynamic resource allocation in cloud computing environments. The target population will consist of cloud service providers and edge computing nodes facing dynamic workloads and user mobility challenges. The evaluation period will span six months, during which the proposed framework will be compared against traditional static optimization strategies and existing MARL approaches. Primary outcomes will include resource utilization efficiency and response time under varying load conditions, while secondary outcomes will assess scalability and user satisfaction metrics. This study aims to provide actionable insights into real-time resource management in cloud computing, addressing critical gaps in existing literature regarding adaptive strategies and practical implementation challenges.
concept_definition:
{
  "Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL)": "A framework where multiple agents learn to optimize their actions through trial and error in a shared environment, adapting their strategies based on the actions and rewards of other agents.",
  "Dynamic Resource Allocation": "The process of distributing computing resources in real-time based on fluctuating workloads and user demands to optimize performance and efficiency.",
  "Hybrid Optimization Techniques": "Methods that combine multiple optimization strategies, such as genetic algorithms and gradient descent, to enhance the performance of resource allocation solutions.",
  "Incentive Mechanisms": "Strategies designed to motivate agents or users to behave in a desired manner, such as rewarding efficient resource usage to improve overall system performance.",
  "Cloud Computing Environments": "Distributed computing environments that provide on-demand access to shared computing resources over the internet, allowing for scalable and flexible resource management.",
  "Resource Utilization Efficiency": "A measure of how effectively computing resources are used, calculated as the ratio of utilized resources to total available resources.",
  "Response Time": "The time taken for a system to respond to a request, crucial for user satisfaction and service quality in cloud computing.",
  "Scalability": "The capability of a system to handle a growing amount of work or its potential to accommodate growth without performance degradation.",
  "User Satisfaction Metrics": "Quantitative measures that assess user contentment with the service provided, often derived from surveys or usage data.",
  "Real-Time Adaptability": "The ability of a system to adjust its operations dynamically in response to changing conditions in the environment, such as varying workloads and user mobility.",
  "Interpretability": "The degree to which a model's predictions can be understood by humans, often assessed through methods like attention visualization or explanation generation.",
  "User Trust": "The confidence users have in the system's reliability and performance, influenced by factors such as perceived transparency and trust calibration."
}

gap: Prior studies have demonstrated the potential of Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) for optimizing resource allocation in cloud computing environments; however, they treat the dynamic nature of workloads and user mobility as secondary, leaving unclear whether real-time adaptability affects resource utilization efficiency and response times. This matters practically because efficient resource management is critical for service quality in cloud environments. Therefore, this study investigates the integration of hybrid optimization techniques and incentive mechanisms within an adaptive MARL framework to enhance dynamic resource allocation in cloud computing.
question: How does the integration of hybrid optimization techniques and incentive mechanisms within an adaptive Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning framework impact resource utilization efficiency and response times in cloud computing environments facing dynamic workloads and user mobility challenges compared to traditional static optimization strategies?
theoretical_mechanism: The independent variable is the integration of hybrid optimization techniques and incentive mechanisms within an adaptive Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework. The mediator is the real-time adaptability of the system, which enhances resource allocation efficiency by dynamically adjusting to changing workloads and user mobility. The dependent variables are resource utilization efficiency and response times in cloud computing environments. The theoretical framework is grounded in adaptive systems theory, which posits that systems can optimize performance through continuous learning and adaptation. System-level outcomes, such as resource utilization efficiency, are influenced by technical mechanisms like adaptive resource allocation algorithms, while user-level outcomes, such as user satisfaction, are mediated by psychological mechanisms like perceived responsiveness. Assumptions that require empirical validation include the effectiveness of incentive mechanisms in promoting desired agent behaviors and the impact of real-time adaptability on overall system performance.
hypothesis: The integration of hybrid optimization techniques and incentive mechanisms within an adaptive Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning framework will significantly improve resource utilization efficiency compared to traditional static optimization strategies, with real-time adaptability mediating this effect.

proposal: This research proposal aims to develop an adaptive Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework integrated with hybrid optimization techniques and incentive mechanisms for dynamic resource allocation in cloud computing environments, specifically targeting cloud service providers and edge computing nodes facing challenges related to fluctuating workloads and user mobility. Key concepts include Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning, dynamic resource allocation, hybrid optimization techniques, and incentive mechanisms, all of which will be operationally defined to enhance clarity. The study is technically feasible, relying on access to open-source MARL models and GPU resources for simulation. The motivation stems from the inadequacies of existing static optimization strategies in addressing real-time adaptability, which is crucial for maintaining service quality in dynamic cloud environments. The literature reveals a significant gap in the scalability and real-world applicability of current MARL approaches, particularly in their treatment of user mobility as a secondary concern. The central research question investigates how the integration of hybrid optimization techniques and incentive mechanisms within an adaptive MARL framework impacts resource utilization efficiency and response times compared to traditional static optimization strategies. The theoretical mechanism posits that the independent variable (integration of hybrid techniques and incentives) enhances real-time adaptability (mediator), leading to improved resource utilization efficiency and response times (dependent variables) through distinct system-level pathways (technical mechanisms) and user-level pathways (user satisfaction). The hypothesis is that this integration will significantly enhance resource utilization efficiency compared to static strategies, with real-time adaptability mediating this effect. Constructs will be operationalized using metrics such as utilization ratios and average response times, with user satisfaction assessed through surveys. The methodology includes a six-month empirical evaluation comparing the proposed framework against traditional methods, controlling for confounding factors like network latency and hardware performance. Expected contributions encompass theoretical advancements in adaptive systems theory, technical innovations in MARL algorithms, empirical insights from rigorous evaluations, and practical deployment guidelines for cloud service providers. Key limitations include potential confounding variables affecting results and ethical considerations regarding user data handling, with a risk analysis identifying failure modes such as dynamic workload mismanagement and user mobility challenges, alongside mitigation strategies to enhance robustness.
